item.title: CVE-2026-62973 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Friday 13 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a remote out-of-bounds read exists in the official BACnet client application apps/readpropm in bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6. When readpropm sends a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request to a malicious BACnet/IP peer, the peer can reply with a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK that drives the client into a global-buffer-overflow read on the global receive buffer Rx_Buf. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-62974 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Friday 13 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. item.title: CVE-2026-63079 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.3

item.title: CVE-2026-95377 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.4
item.description:
Friday 13 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.4 | OS command injection in the TFTP provisioning module of Zenitel EdgeAudioClient before 9.6.3.0, and 10.x before 10.1.3.0, on VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root via a crafted DHCP option 66 (TFTP Server Name) value supplied by a rogue DHCP server on the same network segment. The DHCP-supplied value is passed to a shell without sanitization. Devices using DHCP, the default configuration, are affected on every boot and lease renewal.
The same injection is also reachable via the config_update_tftp_server and sw_update_tftp_server configuration fields by an attacker able to modify the device configuration.

item.title: CVE-2026-95378 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.6
item.description:

This can be escalated to arbitrary code execution as root, for example by overwriting startup scripts or planting SSH keys.

item.title: CVE-2026-121809 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description:
Friday 13 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to occupy a BEAM scheduler indefinitely via a client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming request whose body ends inside a gRPC message.
GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.read_stream/1 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy.ex, and the Cowboy adapter in grpc before the package split) asks for more data whenever the buffer does not hold a complete message. Once the request body has ended, every further read returns an empty chunk, so the buffer never changes and the function retries without end. A single 5-byte length prefix sent with END_STREAM keeps one scheduler busy for as long as the connection stays open, and repeated requests exhaust all schedulers.
This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0; grpc: from 0.3.1 before 1.0.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-124279 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description:
Friday 13 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming requests.
The streaming read clause of GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.Handler.info/3 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy/handler.ex) asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read and compares the running total with max_body_size only after the read returns. The gRPC length prefix of a message is not checked before the message is buffered. Each stream can therefore buffer up to one full read beyond the configured limit before it is refused, and many concurrent streams exhaust node memory. Releases before 1.0.6 apply no limit to streaming requests at all.
This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-128986 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.0
item.description:
Friday 13 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.0 | In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.3, ABAC-enabled deployments match `ROUTE` access rules against the fully decoded request path, while the router routes on the raw, still encoded path. An encoded slash (`%2F`) inside a path value is a segment separator for the access check but part of the value for the router, so a request can match a narrow `ROUTE` rule while the handler returns a different, larger resource.
An authenticated caller whose rules grant READ only on parts of a resource can therefore read the whole resource. In the DPP API, a rule such as `/v1/dpps/*/elements/*`, meant to grant only passport elements, also grants the complete passport whose identifier contains `/elements/`. In the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment, a rule such as `/submodels/*/submodel-elements/*/attachment`, meant to grant only file attachments, also grants the complete element whose stored idShort contains `%2F`.
The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.4.
